name: St. Jakob im Walde
kurzbeschreibung: Highest-lying municipality in Osttirol, surrounded by a secluded mountain landscape in the Lienzer Dolomiten, with a traditional alpine life.
beschreibung:
Overview

St. Jakob im Walde represents the serene, high-altitude mountain farming hamlets and alpine pastures of East Tyrol in the Lienz district, perched at elevations exceeding 1,400 meters. Set against the solitary mountain ramparts of the Lienz Dolomites, the Villgraten Mountains, and the Carnic Ridge, this destination embodies the most remote farming enclaves far from commercial tourism and transit routes. Home to around 270 residents living in historic timber farmsteads and scattered mountain holdings across steep slopes, the area offers total tranquility, crystalline mountain air, and unpolluted night skies. It remains an insider sanctuary for independent travelers, wilderness seekers, long-distance hikers, and ski mountaineers yearning for unspoiled nature.

History

The cultivation of East Tyrol's sunny high-altitude terrain above 1,400 meters dates back to high-medieval Schwaighöfe, dairy estates founded by monastic orders. For centuries, multi-generational farming families endured severe alpine weather, carving out a cultural landscape of terraced mountain meadows and sun-weathered dual-building wooden farmsteads (Paarhöfe). Deep-seated local piety is reflected in wayside shrines, carved crucifixes, and protected wooden chapels standing alongside ancient packhorse paths (such as the historic sanctuary of Maria Schnee in the mountaineering hamlet of Kalkstein). While St. Jakob in Defereggen and St. Johann im Walde represent larger municipal centers elsewhere in East Tyrol, this high-mountain forest farming realm maintains the unvarnished rural heritage of a bygone age, sustained by traditional direct sales of alpine cheese and artisanal farm goods.

Getting there

Reaching these remote high valleys requires driving through the mountain network of the Lienz district. From the north, take the B108 Felbertauern highway through the Felbertauern Tunnel directly to Lienz. From Lienz or South Tyrol, follow federal road B100 along the Drau and Puster valleys towards Sillian, branching off onto winding alpine roads into the Villgraten or Lesach valleys. Rail travelers reach Lienz railway station or local stations at Sillian and Mittewald. Regional VVT buses service the valley villages, with local taxis connecting to upper mountain farmsteads (winter tires and snow chains are essential in winter).

Tips

During winter, the region forms an untouched ski touring paradise: classic routes climb through deep powder onto the panoramic summits of the Villgraten and Carnic mountains without cable car infrastructure. In summer, long-distance hikers can traverse the Carnic Peace Trail (Karnischer Höhenweg) or the celebrated Herz-Ass circuit. Rock climbers will find dramatic via ferratas and limestone walls in the nearby Lienz Dolomites surrounding the Karlsbader Hütte in the Laserzkessel basin. Stop at authentic dairy pastures to sample freshly churned alpine butter, savory grey cheese (Graukäse), and traditional East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen ravioli.
